analysis:
The only change in this PR is one documentation row in docs/provider/cli-reference.md, added at head line 1687. The row documents DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, read in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (`shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey`). `0` disables the load-time shape warmup, and `always` skips the shader-cache probe. The row sits in the table of variables that `darkbloom start` is said to copy into the LaunchAgent plist. No code, wire contract, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage logic changes, so I found no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041, A-001, A-003, A-015 or A-016. The units I reviewed in the base docs (units 4-6) are unchanged context.

Open question for integration: this PR contains only the doc row, so I could not see how the variable is implemented or forwarded. If the warmup runs synthetic prompt shapes, it should use no consumer data. It should also not affect the T-041 prefix-cache scoping, the SSD cache donations, or the TTFT oracle (SEC-035). The doc row may also overstate passthrough: LaunchAgent.swift is not in this batch, so I cannot confirm the variable is actually in `inferencePassthroughEnvKeys`. That would be a documentation accuracy risk, not a security regression. A reviewer of the matching Swift change should check that the warmup is bounded in time and memory, and does not write a cache or use real request content.
